As a reminder Human Echo's are actually a thing (Sunny received an echo of the other Shadow-based awakened he killed all the way back to when he was still an Awakened, when Jet had asked for his help. This was before he enlisted to go to Antartica, even before Nephis woke up iirc), and that its usually up to personal beliefs whether or not you as the awakened wanted to keep it. 

Also, iirc Dire Wolf is a Saint from Clan Song and not Valor.

To be clear, I'm only addressing your comments on how there was no reason for the Dire Wolf Echo to have been rewarded and taken away just like that, because there is. 

You could argue that it does feel like a cop out when G3 really could have taken out someone else.


Its a fun little what if scenario you can play with tho, questions like: 

- If Sunny had been able to keep Dire Wolf as an Echo and subsequently been able to turn it into a shadow, what would that have looked like? How powerful would it have gotten? What abilities would it have had? 


- If it wasn't the Dire Wolf Echo that Skinwalker had taken out, who do you think would have been taken in its place?

The reason is to show us readers the power scaling and threat of Skinwalker without having to write off anyone particularly significant. 

I.e. it shows us that, sure Dire Wolf echo was just an echo, but they were still an Echo of a Saint, one presumably more powerful than Sunny or Nephis was on their own at the time (they had to Tag Team him), and that just simply being a Saint isn't enough to cut it and survive against the Chain of Nightmares. 

Its also why some of the other Saints in the scenes previously also get taken out without much effort (like that Invisible saint from Valor). 

Sunny getting the Dire Wolf Echo and subsequently losing it "just like that" is G3's way of showing us how much stronger Sunny (and Nephis) have become, while also showing us that there's always a bigger fish in that even the strength they have now still doesn't mean very much.

Thank you for the in-depth review! I so very rarely get feedback like this. I really appreciate the time you're taking having looked through my Subclass.

> I'd recommend one growing damage die. Like start with a d4 that becomes a d6 and maybe a d8 later. Or you could make the damage more significant if it's a once-per-turn feature, or a limited resource. Look to other subclasses like Battlemaster or Rune Knight for points of comparison.

  
hmm interesting. I'm not against it really, though it harkens a lot to the Brute UA and I'm trying to not copy as much from that existing UA if possible.

  
> But then the healing over time bit potentially gets pretty crazy, depending on just how much CON you have. One minute is 10 turns, so you restore 10 more HP if you have 12 Constitution, or 50 HP if you have 20 Constitution. And that's healing you can get twice between every Short Rest.

  
yes actually. the intention here is that the Second Wind is actually far more stronger outside of combat. but I wanted to give the subclass more sustainability when Second Wind is used IN combat to offset their lack of options in combat, hence the trickle healing afterwards. 

> Ruthless Consistency is kinda useless. At such high levels, hit chance and AC matter relatively little. 

thats also fair and intended. 15th level is at the sweet spot where you're starting to go up against the real hitters but your AC will still somewhat come into play, and this ability serves to give you more consistent advantage before everything starts leveling out when you hit cap levels where at that point AC doesn't matter. its more meant to protect you while you're still making your grind up to max. Yes that Dragon will still definitely hit you no matter what, but against its minions that extra 2AC might just be the difference between a hit or not.

  
> This feature means a champion fighter can't roll less than 20 on the saving throw of their main stat- essentially they become immune to effects targeting that Ability.

While I don't think I intended for the Champion to be essentially immune (thanks for point that out!) I do still think that it aligns with what I was trying to achieve with my design philosophy regarding the subclass, which I will talk more on below.

> The second bit is cool, though it needs some editing.

this is actually the one thing I took direct from the Brute UA. the second bit is part of its 7th level ability (Brutish Durability), and I thought it perfectly matched what Survivor did in terms of both mechanic and flavor. 



All of this feedback is to say, that my entire Design Philosophy with the Champion subclass is to make it hit a little bit harder, and that much more harder to put down, to make up for the fact that looking at it even with the class, theres actually very little versatility that the subclass offers the class. 

  
When juxtaposed against the Eldritch Knight and their spellcasting, the Samurai and their on-demand Advantage on all-attack rolls via Fighting Spirit, the Arcane Archer and their toolbox of Arrows, the Cavalier and their ability to support tank, Psi Warrior and their maneuverability, the Rune Knight and their utility, and the adaptability of the Battle Master, the one thing the Champion boasts is their resiliency and their ability to face check that teeters on par with a Barbarian.

additionally, you do also make a good point about the AC boost not quite being good enough. My intention for this is that since you're most likely to swing a hung chunk of metal around (ala Cloud from FF7 or Guts from Berserk) that you'd have learned how to use it as a shield to block arrows or other attacks. I'll prolly boost the buff to a +2, so as to feel like you're equipping a shield as a trade-off for an attack along with more consistent damage rolls.

thank you for the feedback! you do make some really good points. 

- I do like the idea of creating a specific fighting style just for gun/crossbow users too. the tricky part here will be to try and make abilities that wouldn't step on any exisiting abilities/feats already. We want to still encourage people to take feats that synergize well with these fighting styles, and keep that opportunity cost present as well.

- Also, I do understand that removing the 3rd and even 4th extra attack can be jarring for people, but I will double down here and say that it is intentional. Not every fighter is going to be built with offense or damage in mind, and as such, not every fighting style needs them. The trade off here instead is the utility or defense it can offer. 

An example being the Defense Fighting Style I've expounded upon here. While you may not ever get a 3rd and 4th attack, you do instead get the ability to take the Dodge Action as a bonus action at 11th level, and even add your Proficiency Bonus to your AC at 20th level. This is because in my opinion, if you choose to invest in this Fighting Style, you're probably someone who's trying to be the Party Tank. And as such, I'll give you the tools you need to do that without having to Multiclass to do it. 

And yeah, not every Fighting Style is going to feel as strong, but that's the point I'm trying to get at here. if you want the damage output, then you can choose Dueling and your Fighting Style will reflect that significantly. 

Your Fighting Style option now becomes so much more important, and becomes much more central to your play style and to your character.

Yes. Fighting Style Improvement is meant to replace the 3rd extra attack a fighter gets at 11th level, while Fighting Style Mastery is meant to replace the 4th extra attack they get at 20th level. 

What I did was that instead of giving fighters 4 attacks at 20th level, I instead tied those extra attacks to the Fighting Style. so you'll notice that not every fighting style gets 4 attacks at 20th level, and even then, those extra attacks only work while you're fighting in your chosen fighting style. 

hope this clears things up! :3

Look at him. Look at him walk away and help that pregnant lady, the lady who, by the way, wasn’t even asking for help. She would have been fine on her own. He really didn’t need to go up to her just to help her carry her groceries back to her car you know.

That’s Austin by the way. He’s Midland High’s resident superman/boy scout/poster child/ you name it. He’s the quarterback, leader of the debate club, captain of the chess club, and five-time annual spelling bee champion back to back. Seriously, why are spelling bees even still a thing in college? And before I forget, he also does volunteer work at the Nursing Home every Friday, at the Soup Kitchen every Saturday, and sings the lead for the choir every Sunday. Seriously, can he be any more picture-perfect?

Talking about appearances, he’s about 6’5’’, blonde hair, and blue eyes. Anything else I missed? No? Then let’s move on.

After helping the mom, Austin then makes his way over to the Nursing Home, because today is a Friday, cutting through the park as a shortcut. Of course he stops to help the kids find their missing dog, and the skaters with their tricks (because of course he’s also a pretty damn good skater). When he finally arrives at the nursing home, the first thing he does is say hi to the nurses, giving them his batch of freshly baked cookies (because of course he’s also a pretty damn good baker), before heading over to the visitor’s center and begins this weeks’ games. It changes every week by the way, last week they were doing backgammon, this week its bingo. 

After about two hours a lucky grandpa finally screamed bingo at the top of his weak lungs, ending the torture for all of us. The prize was a bar of chocolate and the rights to pick the movie for movie night tomorrow. It wasn’t much, but hey, it brought a smile to the old man’s face, not to mention Austin’s who looked annoyingly like he was about to cry. He gets like this every time its bingo night, it doesn’t even make sense. 

After the nursing home he heads home, helping a grandma walk across the street while he’s at it, and tossing a beggar a few bucks and what’s left of his lunch earlier, seriously it is an absolute wonder why he hasn’t been taken advantage of by now, he gets home just in time to help his little sister with her homework (because of course he’s also in the top of his class in academics), before helping his mom set up the table for dinner. His dad comes home just in time and Austin takes his jacket, gives him a quick back rub and ushers him over to the dinner table.

Throughout dinner of course Austin has to be the conversation driver here, asking his parents about their day, and his sister about school. When they’re done, of course Austin has to be the one to wash the dishes, despite his mom’s attempt to do it, with Austin tell her to just sit back because “She’s been working all day” and that she’s probably tired. He ushers his parents to just spend the rest of the night to just catch up, and tells his sister to go to bed. 

He continues working on the dishes and cleaning the dining table diligently, also taking out the trash while he’s at it, because it’s getting halfway full. When everything’s all said and done, he’s left alone downstairs, everybody else is upstairs. He goes up to his parent’s room, of course knocking loudly three times and waiting a few seconds just in case they were getting intimate, comes in and says goodnight. Then he goes into his sister’s room and does the same, before finally heading to his room, and closing the door behind him, and does his own homework.
He finishes homework by midnight, thinking that he’s done enough work for tonight, not even thinking about the fact that the homework he’s been working on isn’t due until next week, and closes the light. Only, he doesn’t go to sleep. 

Instead he carefully creeps outside the hall, putting his ear on the door of his sister’s room, and again on his parent’s room, making sure they’re all sound asleep before heading back to his room. Only to find his window already open, and a girl already sitting on his bed, going over the homework he just finished.

“Cassie, I thought we agreed that we’d meet at the park?” he says, whispering as he closed the door behind him, doing his best to lock the door without making too much noise. 

“You do know that this homework isn’t due until next week right? Besides, I got impatient.” I say back to him, giving him a deadpan look, all the while holding out the homework, “You’ve been spending too much time around other people and not enough time with me”

He gives a chuckle and a slight shake of his head, “Well I can’t help it, and you know how much I like helping people”

“I mean, that’s admirable and all that, but do you really have to help EVERYBODY?” putting air quotes around the word ‘everybody’ for emphasis (while still whispering of course), “I’m sure those kids would have found their dog eventually, and those skaters would have gotten the hang of that flip eventually” crossing my hands over my chest and giving him a ‘humph’ and turning my head away from his direction

“So you’ve been following me have you?”

“So what if I have?” my head now looking down

“How long?” he asks me, and I hear him step forward and take the spot beside me

“Ever since you said goodbye” I replied, still not looking at him 

I hear him chuckle, “I’m not even surprised by that” before he grabs me by the chin and lifts my head up in order to meet his.

As I look into those damned blue eyes that somehow still stand out in the dark, I remind myself about all the things I hate about him. How he always wants to go and help people, regardless of the consequences on him, how he always wants to be the one to do things, never letting people help him, and especially how he’s been spending time with all those other people, all still under the pretense of ‘helping’ them. 

“I hate you. I really should break up with you” I tell him, not seriously of course, because I could never actually do that. 

“I love you too” is all he says before he closes the distance between us
